turns.user: What restrictions does the paper place on the parameters of the Inverse Gaussian, Log-Normal and Gamma distributions of the error term 1 + ϵt in ETS(M,*,*) models, and why?
turns.assistant:
All three are restricted so the multiplicative error has unit mean, E(1 + ϵt) = 1, keeping the model unbiased:

- **Inverse Gaussian**: location μ = 1 (scale σ² free), so mean = μ = 1.
- **Log-Normal**: location μ = −σ²/2, so mean = exp(μ + σ²/2) = 1.
- **Gamma**: shape ξ = 1/σ², so mean = ξσ² = 1.

This unit-mean restriction is what allows these positive distributions to be applied directly to the multiplicative error of conventional ETS(M,*,*) models without log-transforming the model.

**Evidence:**

turns.user: Why do the authors consider the Inverse Gaussian distribution the most convenient of the positive distributions, and what supports that?
turns.assistant:
**Why (W1, C15):**
- Its unit-mean restriction is simple: just set location μ = 1.
- Its scale σ² has a closed-form MLE: (1/T)Σ εₜ²/(1+εₜ) (C6).
- The convolution of i.i.d. Inverse Gaussian variables is well defined.
- By contrast, Log-Normal has a non-convex likelihood with a scale estimate existing only in some cases (C7), and Gamma has no closed-form scale MLE (C18).

**Support:** The argument is explicitly one of convenience, not empirical superiority — the authors note that Folks & Chhikara (1978, B8) found data can be described equally well by all three distributions, and their own simulations show the three perform very similarly (C17). W1 concedes "the argument is not tested."
